subject.title: Model configuration accepts unvalidated model names, enabling silent misconfiguration

question: Should OpenClaw treat configured model refs missing from trusted runtime/catalog evidence as advisory warnings, hard validation failures, or only known-retired/suppressed-model warnings?
rationale: Provider routing, config validation, doctor behavior, and fallback semantics are compatibility-sensitive, and current source shows the remaining fix depends on how much catalog authority maintainers want over custom or newly released model refs.

options.title: Advisory trusted-catalog validation
options.body: Warn in `config validate` and doctor when configured refs are absent from trusted runtime/catalog evidence, while using clear wording for custom and future refs.

options.title: Strict fail-closed validation
options.body: Reject configured refs not present in trusted catalog evidence, reducing runtime surprises but risking upgrade breaks for custom providers and newly released models.

options.title: Keep suppression-only validation
options.body: Continue only blocking known-retired or explicitly suppressed refs, preserving compatibility but leaving the reported silent-misconfiguration class mostly unresolved.

recommendation.title: Advisory trusted-catalog validation
recommendation.body: Warn in `config validate` and doctor when configured refs are absent from trusted runtime/catalog evidence, while using clear wording for custom and future refs.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans model catalog core, fallback observability, and config/doctor policy, and steipete has recent history across the most central surfaces plus timeline activity on this issue.
